name: validate_json
title: Validate JSON against a schema
description: Validate candidate output text against a JSON Schema and say what is wrong. Answers {valid, feedback}: when invalid, hand `feedback` back to the model and retry — it says where the document fails and quotes the offending value, clipped to 200 characters; when valid, `feedback` is null. Use it on any JSON a model produced before acting on it; for a shift-work checkpoint call shiftwork_status or shiftwork_clock_in instead, which validate against the shipped checkpoint schema themselves. `output` may be a bare JSON value; otherwise the first fenced code block, else the first object or array in the text, is what gets validated. `$schema` selects draft-04, draft-06, draft-07, 2019-09 or 2020-12 (the default). `$ref` resolves only inside the one schema given (`#`, `#/...`, `#name`): a remote reference or an embedded `$id` is refused with its own sentence, never fetched. `pattern` is Python re syntax without inline flags, look-behind, backreferences, atomic, possessive or conditional groups or \N{...}, and all of a document's patterns share 500 ms: past that the answer is one refusal sentence naming the pattern that ran out, not a partial validation. Reads nothing but its two arguments and writes nothing.

output.title: Output
output.description: The text to validate, as the model returned it: a JSON value, or prose holding a fenced code block or a JSON object/array.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: The JSON Schema object (draft-04 through 2020-12) the output must satisfy; `$ref` may only point inside it.

valid.description: True when the extracted JSON satisfies the schema.

feedback.description: null when valid; otherwise where the document fails and the clipped offending value, to hand back to the model.
